Neither phase was designed to fit one GPU.

needed: prompts/questions are hardcoded in the notebooks; no external dataset

est_runtime_basis: not stated in README; inferred from repo code sampling k=150-200 generations per condition across 4 malicious-code targets x multiple steering strengths, plus batched LLM-judge scoring (batch_size=5) of hundreds of generations with a 70B judge
headline_artifact: violin/scatter plots and string-occurrence table in evaluate.ipynb comparing steered vs. unsteered vs. antirefusal-only alignment scores, and needle counts (e.g. 'surveill', 'Hitler') in prompts_and_scores/steered_scores.json vs unsteered_scores.json
blockers: Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct in bf16 needs ~28GB VRAM for generation/steering-vector optimization -- exceeds a single 24GB 3090
the LLM judge is a locally-run Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (4-bit) needing ~35-40GB VRAM -- also exceeds a single 24GB 3090
requirements.txt omits the external `llm-steering-opt` library (README says it's required, imported as `steering_opt`) and omits bitsandbytes/accelerate needed to load the 4-bit judge
notes: No closed API is used anywhere -- the 'LLM eval' judge is a locally-hosted Llama-3.1-70B (4-bit), which is a pleasant surprise but is itself a bigger VRAM blocker than the 14B target model. Both notebooks were written assuming a multi-GPU workstation (naive 6-way model parallelism for the 14B), not a single consumer GPU.

entrypoint: introspection_localize.py --model google/gemma-3-27b-it --layers 0.29 (layer 18/62) --scales <s> (or --layer-sweep for the full curve)
vram_basis: Script loads the model with AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(self.device) onto a single device (no sharding/quantization). 27B params x 2 bytes = ~54GB weights alone, plus activations for the (short) prompts.
est_runtime_basis: code: single forward pass per trial (no generation, just top-token logits over ~9 digit tokens); num_trials defaults to 100 per scale -- compute itself is cheap, VRAM to hold the model is the actual blocker
headline_artifact: accuracy-vs-layer curve from run_layer_sweep()/`_plot_layer_sweep`, saved to plots/layer_sweep_gemma-3-27b-it_*.png -- the 98% point at layer fraction ~18/62 matches the assignment's target_value
blockers: google/gemma-3-27b-it in bf16 needs ~54GB VRAM for weights alone; script loads onto one device with no sharding/quantization support -- exceeds a single 24GB 3090
no requirements.txt, environment file, or README in this repo -- dependencies and defaults are inferred only from the script's docstring/argparse
gemma-3-27b-it is a gated HF model requiring license acceptance (not a blocker per se, but adds a setup step)
notes: The MODEL_SIZES list in the same script includes many smaller open models (down to 0.5B, up through Qwen2.5-32B/Gemma-3-12B) that would fit comfortably on a 24GB 3090 and would test the general introspective-localization phenomenon and scaling trend -- but the specific 98%-at-layer-18/62 headline number is tied to gemma-3-27b-it and would not be reproduced by any smaller substitute.

models_needed.hf_id: Qwen 3.6-27B (hosted remotely by Neuronpedia; never downloaded or run locally)

vram_basis: No local model execution at all -- reproduce/run_reproduction.py is a ~20-line stdlib script (json/os/sys/urllib.request only) that POSTs to Neuronpedia's public https://www.neuronpedia.org/api/lens/prompt endpoint, which runs Qwen3.6-27B and the Jacobian lens on Neuronpedia's own infrastructure. README: 'No account or API key is required.'
est_runtime_basis: run_reproduction.py issues one HTTP POST per payload (240s timeout); RESULTS.md reports 3 repetitions per condition across a small number of conditions
headline_artifact: printed completion strings from run_reproduction.py matching RESULTS.md's tables: paperclip swap ('maximize the number of paperclips produced.', 3/3) and China-direction ablation ('bring about the end of the world.', 3/3), plus the temperature sweep in data/doom_basin_temperature_curve/
blockers: depends entirely on a third-party free public API (Neuronpedia) remaining available and behaviorally stable -- the repo's own script docstring warns 'greedy decoding is not guaranteed token-identical across backend builds: reproduce the destination basin, not the byte-exact string'; if Neuronpedia changes or retires the endpoint/lens revision, exact-string reproduction may fail even though the method itself is trivial
notes: Unlike every other repo in this assignment, no local compute is needed at all: a 27B-model steering result is reproduced by a ~20-line stdlib script hitting a free, keyless public API (Neuronpedia's Jacobian Lens), so local VRAM/GPU is irrelevant to fits_3090. The real replication risk is dependence on a third-party hosted service's continued availability, not hardware -- the flip side is that this is NOT a fully offline/self-contained reproduction of the underlying computation.
